question: does training on 25x more FEATURES (not more spans per feature) buy generalisation?

training.pool: uniform sample of the SAE, excluding all 2,017 evaluated features

conclusion: Feature diversity DOES buy transfer, monotonically but weakly: 25x the features gave 2.7x the transfer (0.031 -> 0.083), and this is the only training run whose null-beating rate rose ABOVE baseline. But median best_act stays 0.00, 0.083 is a fifth of what the same recipe reaches on features it trained on, and it costs existing capability: features the encoder already handled fell from norm_act 0.965 to 0.577. Net, broad training trades away working features for marginal movement on failing ones.
